title: release-rollout-checklist-noah-kim
content:
Goal: run a low-risk canary for runtime v1.3.2 (kernel/kv-cache improvements + small batching change).

Context / quick notes:
- This is a user-facing runtime change that can affect latency tail and batch throughput.
- We are targeting Redwood-hosted API first (west1), then dedicated pools if smoke OK.
- Previous canary (v1.3.1) showed small 95p latency regression for long-seq workloads; watch sequence-length-tagged metrics closely.

High-level plan (quick):
1) Create canary route/traffic split (hosted-api route): 1% -> v1.3.2, 99% -> stable (v1.2.9).
2) Monitor for 30m at 1% baseline, then 10% for 1h, then 25% for 2h if all green, then consider ramp to 50%/75%/100% by business hours schedule.
3) Pinning notes: update rollout config and add explicit pin for enterprise customers flagged w/commit id if requested.
4) If any alert triggers (see criteria), rollback to v1.2.9 immediately and open incident.

Checklist (hands-on)
- [ ] Branch & release: tag platform/runtime v1.3.2 (done by release-engineering). Confirm binary SHA: sha256:abc123def456.
- [ ] Build & smoke locally: run micro-bench for kv-cache on test suite (results attached in PR).
- [ ] Update route config: /v1/generate canary -> traffic config (1%).
- [ ] Update deployment manifest: add new image and canary label (release: v1.3.2-canary).
- [ ] Notify SRE + Oncall + CS: post to #releases + #oncall 15m before flip.
- [ ] Start canary at 03:00 UTC (low-traffic window).
- [ ] Record baseline metrics in notes (95p latency, errors, CPU/GPU utilization).
- [ ] Run smoke tests and end-to-end prompts through canary route (sample prompts list below).
- [ ] If stable after thresholds, follow ramp schedule.

Rollout percentages and timing (suggested)
- Step 0: 0% -> prepare (smoke & tests)
- Step 1: 1% for 30 minutes (basic checks)
- Step 2: 10% for 60 minutes (look for statistical signals)
- Step 3: 25% for 120 minutes (business-hours monitoring)
- Step 4: 50% for 3 hours
- Step 5: 75% for 4 hours
- Step 6: 100% (promote and close rollout)

Monitoring / signals to watch (explicit)
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) for candidate route vs baseline (segment by seq_len > 1024). Query: datadog/monitoring shorthand: "avg:last_5m:trace.duration{route:generate,env:prod,version:v1.3.2} by {percentile, seq_len_bucket}"
- Error rate: 5xx / request failures > 0.5% absolute increase = alert.
- OOMs / GPU memory errors in logs (grep for "OOM" or "cuda error").
- Quality regressions: sample eval set (10 canonical prompts) - compare top-1 outputs for token-level drift and hallucination markers.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and GPU saturation (expect slight increase in GPU usage, <10%).
- Cold-start failures and model load time increases > 200ms.

Rollback criteria (immediate)
- Any uncaught 5xx spike > 1% absolute vs baseline for 5m.
- p99 latency increase > 2x baseline for 10m or sustained p95 > SLA (2s) for 10m.
- Reproducible quality regression on canonical eval set (manual verification).
- Any SRE oncall escalation requesting rollback.

Pinning / enterprise customer notes
- For customers on dedicated pools, we will not force upgrade. Add new config in customer pins table if requested: customer_pin = {customer_id: X, runtime_version: v1.3.2, forced: false}.
- For private/VPC customers who requested patch, coordinate with solutions-eng to bundle the binary and provide upgrade instructions.

Commands & quick ops snippets
- Update route traffic config (kubectl/app-config example):
  kubectl apply -f canary-traffic-v1.3.2.yaml  # sets traffic split 99/1
- Rollback (quick):
  kubectl apply -f canary-traffic-v1.2.9-restore.yaml
  AND post to #releases: "rollback: runtime v1.3.2 -> v1.2.9 (reason: <short>)"

Smoke test prompts (run through canary):
- short completion: "Summarize: Redwood Inference mission"
- long-seq prompt: 2500-token generation: repeat/test sequence-length edge cases
- structured output: function calling stub -> verify JSON schema consistency

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Need to confirm if batching config default changed affects small-request latencies. If yes, maybe limit canary to less aggressive batching.
- Add Datadog dashboard widget that directly compares v1.3.2 vs v1.2.9 for p50/p95/p99 by seq_len.
- Confirm whether dedupe cache TTL changed - ask product for expected behavior.

Post-rollout follow-up (if promoted)
- Update release notes (Confluence) w/bench results, observed tail behavior, and any config toggles.
- Schedule a short retro with SRE + runtime team to capture lessons.

History / notes from previous canary v1.3.1:
- Observed p95 +8% on >1024-seq during peak 2h window; mitigated by tuning kv-cache eviction. Keep an eye for similar pattern.

Contact list for escalation:
- Oncall SRE: Ethan Wright (primary), Maya Thompson (secondary)
- Runtime owner: Zoe Ramirez
- Release engineer: Noah Kim (me)

Quick log (timestamps) - example format to copy into incident notes:
- 2025-11-12 03:00 UTC - flipped 1% -> v1.3.2
- 2025-11-12 03:30 UTC - increased to 10% after no regressions
- 2025-11-12 04:40 UTC - observed p99 spike on seq_len>2048, rolled back at 04:55 UTC

-- end of scratchpad (keep this as working doc)
